summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with severe right ankle pain and swelling, initially concerning for septic arthritis. Arthrocentesis revealed purulent fluid with over 400,000 WBCs and monosodium urate crystals, leading to a diagnosis of gout. Blood and synovial fluid cultures were negative, supporting gout over infection. She was treated with a short course of IV antibiotics, which were discontinued after 48 hours due to clinical improvement and negative cultures. Treatment included prednisone, colchicine, and acetaminophen, with morphine for breakthrough pain. She experienced an asymptomatic episode of hypotension on hospital day 2, managed with fluid bolus and temporary hold of antihypertensives. Her GERD symptoms resolved with continued protonix. She improved steadily, with reduced pain, swelling, and inflammation markers, and was discharged to extended care with plans to start allopurinol after flare resolution and podiatry follow-up for heel pain.
